learningObjective: Identify the aliasing precondition required for loop-invariant code motion to be semantics-preserving in an imperative tensor IR.

canonicalClaims.claim: LICM is only sound when the expression being hoisted has no read that could be modified inside the loop body — this requires alias analysis to prove that in-loop stores do not overlap the invariant's inputs.
conditions: The IR represents memory reads/writes explicitly (not purely functional).
Alias analysis is available (or a conservative may-alias check is used).
nonImplications: Does not imply LICM is unsafe in pure/SSA IRs (there is no aliasing to worry about).
Does not imply that pass ordering with alias analysis is unique; different pipelines can prove the same fact by different means.

sourceMappings.locator: Ch. on loop optimizations; LICM safety

misconceptions.claim: LICM is only valid when the loop trip count is a compile-time constant.
misconceptions.whyWrong: LICM validity is about the semantics of the hoisted computation, not the trip count; loops with symbolic bounds can still be transformed.

misconceptions.claim: Floating-point loop-invariant expressions can never be hoisted because it changes rounding order.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Hoisting a single invariant expression evaluates it once; each iteration in the original loop also observed the same value. The rounding order does not change (unlike, say, reordering an accumulation).
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: Engineering a Compiler; LLVM LangRef (FP flags for reassociation)

misconceptions.claim: LICM does not need alias analysis in an SSA IR.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Pure SSA over scalar values does not need it, but LICM on IRs with load/store operations (memref-like, PyTorch tensors with in-place ops) still needs alias/dependence reasoning.

misconceptions.claim: LICM always improves performance because it reduces work inside the loop.
misconceptions.whyWrong: LICM can increase register pressure and lengthen live ranges; if it spills, it can slow the code down. It is a heuristic decision, not a strict improvement.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: Engineering a Compiler, Ch. Register allocation

implementationFacts: Alias analysis and dependence analysis are prerequisites for LICM on IRs with memory ops.
LICM is often paired with register-pressure heuristics because hoisted values become longer-lived.
performanceScenarios: In tensor IRs like MLIR affine or linalg-on-tensors, hoisting shape queries or scalar reductions out of tile loops is a common form of LICM.
